name: Unipol Assicurazioni S.p.A.
executive_summary: Unipol Assicurazioni S.p.A. (UNI.MI) screens as a **buy** on the quantitative value framework: nine of 22 models pass (composite 57%), spanning cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk families, at roughly 12× earnings, 2.1× book, 3.9% yield, and 17% ROE. The investment case rests on Italy’s leading non-life franchise, a multi-year earnings recovery, and a capital-return policy that management has recently reinforced (including a raised dividend floor of €930m on H1 2026 results). The central debate is whether reported profitability and cash generation are sustainable once investment-mark volatility and recurring asset impairments are stripped out, and whether the market is adequately discounting catastrophe, regulatory, and Italian macro risk. Primary regulatory filings were not retrieved in this research pack, so conviction rests heavily on Yahoo financials and earnings-call summaries rather than audited filing extracts.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Unipol offers a rare combination in European financials: inexpensive multiples on improving underlying earnings, a visible dividend, and balance-sheet metrics that the screen reads as conservative (debt/equity ~41%, current ratio ~4.0). The screen passes Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Lynch PEG, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, and Earnings Quality — a profile consistent with a profitable, cash-generative insurer trading below deep-quality thresholds rather than deep distress.

Business quality, as inferred from secondary sources, appears solid: news summaries describe improved combined ratios, motor underwriting on track, and robust solvency through 2025–H1 2026. Yahoo data (fallback) show revenue rising from €10.0bn (2022) to €13.7bn (2025) and normalized income from €824m to €2.03bn over the same period, supporting the screen’s earnings-growth and quality signals. Free cash flow rebounded sharply to €4.05bn in 2025 (operating cash flow €4.59bn), which underpins FCF Yield and dividend models despite the screen flagging weak “financial health” liquidity scoring — a known quirk for asset-heavy insurers where headline current ratios are less informative than solvency coverage.

What the screen does *not* fully capture — and where value investors must do more work — is the earnings quality behind large recurring “impairment of capital assets” and investment-security mark-to-market swings, plus the absence of verified Solvency II ratios from primary filings in this pack. The buy case is therefore “quality compounder at a reasonable price with income,” not “deep value net-net” (failed Graham Net-Net, Schloss, Deep Value) or “wide moat” (ROE 16.9% sits just below the screen’s 18% moat hurdle).
financial_review:
**Primary filings:** The `filings_index.json` catalogue contains **zero** entries (no annual reports, half-year results, trading updates, or body extracts under `filings/bodies/`). Annual and interim regulatory analysis cannot be grounded in filing text for this pass. All quantitative trends below fall back to **Yahoo `financials_annual.json`**, with recent operational colour drawn only from news summaries (not filing bodies).

**Annual trends (Yahoo fallback, EUR):**

| Metric | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|--------|------|------|------|------|
| Total revenue | €10.0bn | €12.4bn | €13.2bn | €13.7bn |
| Reported net income | €525m | €1.10bn | €1.07bn | €1.48bn |
| Normalized income | €824m | €1.53bn | €1.74bn | €2.03bn |
| Diluted EPS | €0.73 | €1.54 | €1.50 | €2.03 |
| Operating cash flow | €1.72bn | €1.54bn | €2.52bn | €4.59bn |
| Free cash flow | €905m | €244m | €1.59bn | €4.05bn |
| Cash dividends paid | €321m | €388m | €350m | €953m |

Revenue has compounded steadily, and normalized earnings have nearly doubled since 2022, but **reported** net income remains volatile: each year includes substantial “special income charges” and impairments of capital assets (€388m–€799m annually in 2022–2024; €740m in 2025), which depress statutory profit relative to normalized figures. Investment-related volatility is material — gain/loss on investment securities swung from +€1.33bn (2022) to −€3.37bn (2023) to −€535m (2024) to −€2.28bn (2025) per Yahoo cash-flow classification — consistent with a large fair-value-through-P&L portfolio (financial assets designated FVTPL ~€21.5bn at end-2025 on a €90.4bn asset base).

**Balance sheet (Yahoo fallback, end-2025):** Total assets €90.4bn; common equity €10.4bn; tangible book €7.75bn; total long-term debt €5.01bn; net debt €3.83bn. The balance sheet is investment-dominated (investments and advances ~€74.4bn), typical of a European insurer but amplifying mark-to-market sensitivity. Equity has grown from €6.86bn (2022) to €10.39bn (2025), supporting the screen’s quality and ROE signals.

**Cash conversion and dividends:** 2025 FCF of €4.05bn comfortably covered cash dividends of €953m (Yahoo), though the 2023 FCF trough (€244m) illustrates that insurer cash flows can be lumpy when working-capital and investment realisations move. The screen’s TTM FCF (~$2.05bn in snapshot currency) and operating cash flow ($4.59bn) align directionally with the 2025 Yahoo spike but should be treated cautiously without filing reconciliation.

**Interim / recent periods:** No interim filing bodies are indexed. News summaries (secondary) indicate:
- **Q3 2025** (7 Nov 2025): nine-month net profit ~€1.12bn; motor metrics improving.
- **FY/Q4 2025** (20 Feb 2026): consolidated results >€1.5bn; solid dividend proposed despite natural-catastrophe impacts.
- **Q1 2026** (16 May 2026): strong solvency, favourable combined ratio; lower investment income.
- **H1/Q2 2026** (7 Aug 2026): net profit “surges”; improved combined ratio; dividend floor raised to **€930m**.

These interim headlines are directionally consistent with the Yahoo annual progression but **cannot be verified** against filing extracts in this pack. Quarterly income in `financials_annual.json` is empty.

**Gaps:** No annual report, half-year report, Solvency II disclosure, segment underwriting detail, or contingency/going-concern language from primary filings. Verify-before-trade should prioritise Borsa Italiana / company IR PDFs and the consolidated statutory accounts.
risks_and_flags:
**Regulatory and solvency:** As a Solvency II insurer, capital requirements, reserving standards, and dividend constraints depend on regulatory ratios not available in this pack. News references “robust solvency,” but without filing bodies this cannot be stress-tested.

**Investment and earnings quality:** Large FVTPL portfolios and recurring impairments (€525m–€799m in 2022–2024 per Yahoo) mean reported earnings are sensitive to rates, credit spreads, and equity markets. Normalized income exceeds reported net income in every year shown — a persistent gap that warrants scrutiny for conservative reserving versus aggressive normalization.

**Cyclical underwriting:** Motor insurance dominates the narrative in news summaries. Combined-ratio improvement is positive, but Italian motor remains competitive and catastrophe-exposed (FY 2025 commentary cites nat-cat impacts). A deterioration in claims frequency, severity, or pricing would compress ROE toward the screen’s failed Economic Moat threshold.

**Leverage and liquidity:** Screen debt/equity ~41% and net debt ~€3.8bn are manageable relative to equity, but insurer “liquidity” is structurally opaque; the screen’s Financial Health fail on weak liquidity and Piotroski F-Score 6/9 (current ratio, gross margin, asset turnover not improving) are yellow flags for trend quality, even if levels look adequate.

**Governance and group complexity:** Unipol operates as part of a broader group (banking, asset management, services). Without filing notes, related-party exposures, segment capital allocation, and minority interests (€324m minority interest at end-2025) cannot be fully assessed.

**Competitive:** Italian insurance consolidation and digital distribution pressure incumbents; Unipol’s scale is an advantage but not immunity.

**Missing filing language:** No going-concern, covenant, litigation, or pension disclosures could be reviewed — a material gap for a financials deep-dive.

RiskTags: regulatory, cyclical, competitive, accounting, leverage

research_rationale: Directional evidence from Yahoo financials and earnings-call summaries supports the screen’s buy signal on valuation, quality, and dividend, but the complete absence of primary filing extracts prevents verification of solvency, reserve adequacy, and earnings adjustments, keeping conviction below full confirmation.
